title: Global sensitivity analysis of the design (Morris)
question: Which parameters is the game's balance most sensitive to?

seeds.note: the same 50 seeds at every design point (common random numbers)

design.method: Morris elementary effects (numpy; SALib not installed)
design.unit_to_value: default × (0.7 + 0.6u); z: 1 − (1 − z₀)(0.7 + 0.6u); fee rounded to the cent

metric_definitions.oracle_win: ORACLE manifesto + ORACLE planner win rate over the 50 seeds
metric_definitions.worker_best: best-channel share: share of seeds whose best paid pattern (by E, among pay_workers, front_workers, pay_media, pay_split; ORACLE manifesto) is pay_workers or front_workers
metric_definitions.media_best: share of seeds whose best paid pattern is pay_media
metric_definitions.EE: [y(x ± Δe_i) − y(x)]·(±1)/Δ with Δ = 2/3 of the box (unit scale)
metric_definitions.mu_star: mean |EE| over the r trajectories; mu = signed mean; sigma = sd (interaction/non-linearity)
metric_definitions.noise_floor_ee_se: mean over all EEs of sd(per-seed EE)/√50 (seed-sampling SE of one EE)
metric_definitions.above_noise: factors whose μ* bootstrap CI lower bound exceeds 2 × noise floor

prediction: none registered (predictions.md: the plan gives no Predict line for X22)
deviations: z box on the margin 1 − z (z ∈ [0.7725, 0.8775]) because the literal ±30% box reaches z = 1.07 > 1.
'best-channel share' operationalised as the share of seeds where a worker-only pattern is the best paid pattern (media-best share also reported).
Sobol indices (optional in the plan) not computed.
Electorates drawn on the GPU (generation='device'); parity uses the canonical CPU draw.
